mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for FEDFUNDS as a predictor of 20-day SPX returns falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the average 20-day return in periods with declining FEDFUNDS is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the unemployment rate exceeding 0.5 percentage points from the prior month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which triggers a short-term flight to safety and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 5-day SPX return following UNRATE increases > 0.5pp is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC for UNRATE as a 5-day predictor is below 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in both residential investment (HOUST) and consumer spending (RSAFS) indicate a broad-based demand contraction, which signals an impending recession and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction term (HOUST and RSAFS both declining) fails to predict negative 60-day SPX returns with a Rank IC above 0.03 in any 3-year rolling window, or the average 60-day return in interaction-triggered periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During periods of manufacturing supply chain disruption (INDPRO below 90), a concurrent decline in industrial production growth signals a severe supply shock, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 20-day SPX return in INDPRO < 90 periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC for INDPRO in this regime is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising consumer spending trend (RSAFS) indicates strong household demand, which supports corporate revenue growth and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for RSAFS as a 5-day predictor of SPX returns is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or the average 5-day return in periods of rising RSAFS is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.0% per annum signals a tightening monetary policy cycle, which increases borrowing costs and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 60-day SPX return following FEDFUNDS > 4.0% is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC for FEDFUNDS as a 60-day predictor is below 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in both employment growth (PAYEMS) and labor force participation (UNRATE rising) indicate a weakening labor market, which signals reduced consumer spending power and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction term (PAYEMS declining and UNRATE rising) fails to predict negative 20-day SPX returns with a Rank IC above 0.03 in any 3-year rolling window, or the average 20-day return in interaction-triggered periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In periods of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3.0% year-over-year), a decline in the federal funds rate signals an aggressive monetary easing response, which initially boosts equity markets and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 5-day SPX return in CPIAUCSL > 3.0% periods with declining FEDFUNDS is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC for FEDFUNDS in this regime is below 0.03 over any 2-year window.
